correctness.rationale: In a spider, a geodesic uses edges from at most two arms. Three chosen edges in one arm violate edge general position, and if two chosen edges lie in one arm then any chosen edge in another arm lies with them on a cross-arm geodesic. Conversely, at most one chosen edge per arm, or exactly two chosen edges in one arm and none elsewhere, puts at most two chosen edges on every geodesic. The enumerator and maximal-set counts then follow directly. A fresh independent literal shortest-path replay on representative three- and four-arm spiders matched the characterization; the all-orders claim rests on the geodesic proof, not the finite replay.
residual_risks: The theorem is specific to spiders; no extension to arbitrary branching trees is claimed.
